title: Reiterative Feedback Mechanism (RFM)
use_cases: Implement when using small open-source LLMs that struggle with complex, multi-faceted prompts
Configure when seeking to improve the emotional depth and linguistic quality of generated creative writing
Use when a structured, multi-step feedback loop is required to refine initial model drafts
Apply when needing to stabilize output quality across multiple narrative metrics like creativity and prose flow
content: The Reiterative Feedback Mechanism (RFM) is an iterative framework developed to improve the quality of flash fiction generated by large language models (LLMs), particularly through repeated cycles of draft refinement guided by targeted evaluator feedback.[1] It addresses limitations in baseline LLM outputs, such as predictability and limited creativity, by incrementally enhancing drafts across specific narrative dimensions.[1] RFM employs a straightforward architecture centered on two LLMs: a generator model, typically Llama-2-7B, responsible for producing and revising story drafts, and an evaluator model, Gemini-1.5-pro-latest, which provides structured critique.[1] The process begins with an initial prompt fed to the generator to create a baseline draft. The evaluator then assesses this draft against a predefined set of metrics, selecting one metric per iteration to maintain focus and prevent overload on smaller models.[1] Feedback incorporates rhetorical strategies drawn from exemplary flash fiction and is synthesized with the prior prompt to form a refined instruction for the next generation cycle. This loop repeats until all targeted metrics have been addressed, resulting in a progressively refined narrative.[1] Key targeted metrics include emotional depth (evaluating the complexity and engagement of emotions), linguistic quality (assessing prose flow, elegance, and descriptiveness), and adherence to the original prompt.[1] By concentrating on a single metric per iteration, RFM enables consistent incremental improvements, particularly beneficial for small open-source LLMs like Llama-2-7B and Zephyr-1.6B, which struggle with processing overly complex or multifaceted prompts simultaneously.[1] Evaluation of RFM outputs combined automated scoring via the Anthropic Claude 3 Opus API across 44 dimensions (scaled to a maximum of 100) and manual human assessments of overall quality, creativity, and emotional expression (also scaled to 100).[1] In experiments, RFM improved median scores compared to baselines: for Llama-2-7B, the baseline median rose from 37.2 to 42.5, while for Zephyr-1.6B, it increased from 22.1 to 37.6.[1] Qualitative analysis highlighted gains in creativity, technique, and emotional expression, with RFM demonstrating particular stability and effectiveness on smaller models due to the external evaluator's guidance.[1] Compared to more modular alternatives like MFER, RFM offers greater consistency, especially with tiny language models, though it may yield slightly lower peak emotional depth or overall quality in some cases.[1] The framework's reliance on focus
